question: Why must you clean a surface with soap and water before you use a chemical disinfectant on it?

options.A: Soap and water permanently sterilize all medical instruments
options.B: Water is required to activate the chemical smell of the disinfectant
options.C: Visible dirt and organic matter can block disinfectants from killing germs
options.D: Chemical disinfectants will evaporate too quickly on a dry surface

explanation: You're doing great! Think of dirt or blood as a shield; if it's sitting on the surface, the disinfectant can't actually reach the germs underneath. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary role of a nurse acting as a patient advocate?

options.A: Refusing to talk with doctors about care plans
options.B: Suing the hospital administration whenever there is a treatment delay
options.C: Protecting the patient's rights, safety, and dignity when they cannot speak for themselves
options.D: Making all final medical decisions on behalf of the family

explanation: Brilliant! Being an advocate means standing up for your patients and keeping their best interests at heart. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h7)

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping fast after surgery but waits hours to tell the doctor. What went wrong here?

options.A: Violating patient confidentiality during shift handoff
options.B: Failure to monitor and report critical changes promptly
options.C: Failing to purchase individual liability insurance
options.D: Inappropriate use of electronic health record templates

explanation: Catching changes is only half the job—reporting them quickly to the medical team is vital to keeping patients safe and avoiding liability. [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h7)

question: Which sampling technique simply grabs participants because they are easy to reach and right in front of you?

options.A: Systematic sampling
options.B: Stratified sampling
options.C: Cluster sampling
options.D: Convenience sampling

explanation: Spot on! Convenience sampling uses whoever is readily available—like patients sitting right now in your clinic waiting room. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T17#GNS224_U1_T17_h5)

question: What should a nurse researcher do if their new results don't match older studies?

options.A: Hide the contradictory data so the paper gets published
options.B: Explore potential reasons for the differences in findings
options.C: Change the original hypothesis to match the old literature
options.D: Assume all previous researchers made mistakes in math

explanation: Exactly! Science grows when we look closely at *why* results differ—maybe times have changed, or the patient group is different. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T5#GNS224_U2_T5_h3)

question: A nurse feels stressed because personal values clash with an assigned care duty. What type of conflict is this?

options.A: Intrapersonal conflict
options.B: Interpersonal conflict
options.C: Intragroup conflict
options.D: Intergroup conflict

explanation: When the battle is inside your own head regarding your values and duties, it's an intrapersonal conflict. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of an administrative control?

options.A: Rotating staff away from high-noise areas to limit exposure time
options.B: Replacing a toxic cleaning fluid with warm water and soap
options.C: Providing heavy leather boots to construction workers
options.D: Installing a heavy glass shield around a loud machine

explanation: Changing work schedules and rotating job duties to limit exposure time are classic administrative controls. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is the biggest danger of pulling a Guinea worm out too fast?

options.A: The worm may snap, causing severe inflammation and infection
options.B: The patient will instantly lose consciousness from shock
options.C: The infection will immediately spread to other family members
options.D: The remaining worm will travel directly to the patient's heart

explanation: You nailed it! If the worm breaks, the leftover piece causes a nasty immune reaction and infection. Slow and steady wins the race in nursing procedures! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h6)

question: Which of these is a direct cost for a patient admitted to the surgical ward?

options.A: The general lighting bill for the hospital parking lot
options.B: The monthly salary of the hospital accountant
options.C: The specific surgical gloves worn during their operation
options.D: The cost of repairing the main hospital elevator

explanation: Because those gloves were used directly for that single patient's surgery, they count as a direct cost. Makes total sense when you picture it in the theater! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h2)

question: A patient keeps visiting the clinic with headaches and stomach upset, but all lab tests come out normal. What should you suspect?

options.A: Unresolved psychological stress manifesting as physical symptoms
options.B: A severe vitamin deficiency requiring immediate surgery
options.C: An accidental poisoning caused by community water supply
options.D: A rare tropical infection that laboratory tests cannot detect

explanation: When the lab results are completely clear but the pain is real, the body is often speaking the language of unexpressed stress (somatization). [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the big danger of planning a quality improvement project without asking bedside staff?

options.A: The proposed changes might be totally unworkable in busy clinical practice
options.B: Printing educational brochures will break the budget
options.C: Patients will stop taking their drugs completely
options.D: The hospital will instantly lose its official license

explanation: So true! Management might draw up rules that look amazing on paper, but if they don't fit the chaotic reality of a busy shift, they won't work. Always consult the bedside! [learn more](GST319_U1_T4#GST319_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is it important to ask a patient about their job and workplace environment during a social history?

options.A: It helps calculate the exact monthly income of the patient
options.B: It determines how many days off work the patient needs
options.C: Certain jobs expose workers to toxins that cause chronic illness
options.D: It shows whether the patient enjoys their daily job duties

explanation: Well reasoned! Workplace exposures like dust, fumes, or heavy lifting often play a big role in lung or body pains. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h6)

question: As a community nurse in a malaria-prone area, which prevention tip should you push the hardest?

options.A: Avoiding all outdoor sunlight exposure
options.B: Taking daily high-dose antibiotics
options.C: Using insecticide-treated bed nets
options.D: Drinking boiled milk every morning

explanation: Brilliant! Since malaria mosquitoes love to bite at night while people sleep, treated bed nets are a lifesaver in our communities. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is a major benefit of regular physical activity for older adults?

options.A: Elimination of the need for daily sleep
options.B: Complete reversal of all age-related wrinkles
options.C: Immediate restoration of lost hearing ability
options.D: Improved balance, muscle strength, and mood

explanation: Movement is medicine! Even light, tailored exercise helps seniors stay strong, lowers their risk of falls, and keeps their spirits high. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h6)

question: When can a patient typically start a new method of birth control after a medical abortion?

options.A: Only after waiting for three full menstrual cycles
options.B: Before taking the initial dose of mifepristone
options.C: Six months after the procedure is completed
options.D: Immediately or at the follow-up visit

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! Most birth control methods can be started right away on the day the abortion process is complete. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h7)

question: A patient wants to leave the ward early because they cannot afford their remaining hospital bill. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Connect the patient with the hospital social welfare unit or available support schemes
options.B: Threaten to call security if the patient attempts to leave the bed
options.C: Ignore the situation since financial matters are strictly administrative
options.D: Pay the hospital bill directly out of the nurse's personal salary

explanation: Well done! Hospital social workers are there to help bridge financial gaps and find workable payment solutions so patients can finish their care safely. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T15#GNS312_U4_T15_h2)

question: What does empowerment mean in the context of community mobilisation?

options.A: Building local capacity to solve health problems independently
options.B: Giving financial loans to every household in the village
options.C: Allowing nurses to make all decisions without community input
options.D: Handing out free medicine during festival seasons

explanation: Empowerment equips community members with the skills and confidence to address their own health challenges long-term. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the clearest sign that a community health project has achieved sustainability?

options.A: International donors continue sending large sums of money
options.B: The primary health clinic closes down due to lack of patients
options.C: The local government takes over the salaries of all foreign staff
options.D: The community continues health practices after project staff leave

explanation: You got it! Sustainability means the good habits and programs keep running successfully even after external helpers have packed up and gone home. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h7)

question: In which specific part of the fallopian tube does fertilization normally occur?

options.A: Cervix
options.B: Isthmus
options.C: Ampulla
options.D: Fimbriae

explanation: The ampulla is the wider, middle section of the fallopian tube where the sperm typically meets and fertilizes the released egg. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h2)

question: Which imaging test is generally considered the best for viewing tissue death and fluid collections in acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Standard chest X-ray
options.B: Basic abdominal ultrasound
options.C: CT scan with contrast
options.D: Electrocardiogram strip

explanation: You got it! A contrast CT gives doctors the clearest pictures to spot inflammation, dead tissue, and hidden pockets of fluid around the pancreas. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h5)

question: A patient has a hard mass of stool stuck in the rectum (impaction), yet they keep passing small amounts of liquid. Why does this happen?

options.A: Infection has completely liquefied the entire colon
options.B: Liquid stool leaks around the solid blocked mass
options.C: The small intestine is hyperactive and rushing food
options.D: The kidneys are producing excessive fluid waste

explanation: Don't let this trick you in the ward! Liquid waste from higher up in the gut finds a way to slip past the hard, blocked stool, which can easily look like normal diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which action shows a wonderful balance of efficiency, effectiveness, and equity in a local health program?

options.A: Saving money by refusing to treat patients who cannot pay cash on arrival
options.B: Using low-cost, proven malaria treatments distributed freely to pregnant women in remote villages
options.C: Employing double the required staff for every shift to ensure nobody feels rushed
options.D: Purchasing expensive imported machines that only wealthy patients in the capital can afford

explanation: Brilliant! This uses funds wisely (efficiency), cures malaria reliably (effectiveness), and reaches mothers who need it most for free (equity). [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the main building block your body uses to make all female sex hormones?

options.A: Cholesterol
options.B: Amino acids
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Triglycerides

explanation: Think of cholesterol as the parent molecule! Without it, the body couldn't build vital steroid hormones like estrogen and progesterone. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h1)

question: What is the main focus of efficiency in a healthcare plan?

options.A: Getting maximum results with minimum waste of resources
options.B: Spending the entire annual budget before the year ends
options.C: Employing as many administrative workers as possible
options.D: Purchasing the most expensive medical equipment available

explanation: Efficiency is all about making the best use of limited supplies, money, and staff time without unnecessary waste. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h6)

question: In traditional Nigerian societies, what was usually believed to be the main cause of severe mental illness?

options.A: Degeneration of brain cells from aging
options.B: A deficiency of essential dietary vitamins
options.C: Spiritual forces and ancestral influences
options.D: Genetic mutations passed down generations

explanation: Spot on! Historically, communities often connected deep emotional or psychological struggles to spiritual factors, witchcraft, or broken taboos rather than biological causes. You've got this! [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h1)

question: How does government-funded agricultural research benefit the general public?

options.A: By ensuring that farming requires zero human labor input
options.B: By developing pest-resistant crops that secure the food supply
options.C: By removing all regulations on chemical pesticide usage
options.D: By discovering new ways to make processed foods last indefinitely

explanation: Research creates stronger, higher-yield crops that protect against harvest failures and maintain stable food availability. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h3)

question: What is a key question a nurse can ask to assess food security in a patient?

options.A: What is your exact family income down to the last dollar?
options.B: Do you prefer eating white bread or whole grain bread?
options.C: Do you worry about running out of food before getting more money?
options.D: How many hours of physical exercise do you do each week?

explanation: Screening for food security involves asking direct, simple questions about running out of food and lacking money to buy more. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h8)

question: During which stage of an infection do mild, general symptoms like tiredness first show up before full sickness hits?

options.A: Incubation period
options.B: Prodromal stage
options.C: Convalescent stage
options.D: Illness stage

explanation: Well done! The prodromal stage is that early phase where a patient just feels 'off' or unusually tired before specific symptoms appear. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h6)

question: How does school management help promote health teaching in the classroom?

options.A: By banning discussions about personal hygiene and nutrition
options.B: By ensuring health education is properly timetabled and resourced
options.C: By personally teaching every biology class in the school
options.D: By leaving health teaching entirely up to extracurricular clubs

explanation: Spot on! Management sets up the timetable and supplies the learning materials so teachers can teach health topics effectively. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h5)

question: What type of variation is expected, normal, and just part of everyday clinical processes?

options.A: Artificial data corruption
options.B: Catastrophic system failure
options.C: Common cause variation
options.D: Special cause variation

explanation: Common cause variation is just the everyday, normal ups and downs that happen naturally in any routine task. [learn more](GST319_U2_T7#GST319_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is a great action for a nurse giving Psychological First Aid to a disaster survivor?

options.A: Insisting that they share their deepest fears before receiving water
options.B: Leaving them completely alone until a psychiatrist arrives on duty
options.C: Connecting the person with family members and basic survival needs
options.D: Telling the person that everything happens for a reason immediately

explanation: You nailed it! Helping survivors find loved ones, water, and shelter is the heart of effective Psychological First Aid. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T3#GNS315_U1_T3_h7)

question: What makes a nursing care plan truly 'individualized' in holistic practice?

options.A: Writing the care plan in medical jargon the patient cannot understand
options.B: Leaving all care planning decisions entirely up to the attending physician
options.C: Using the exact same printed template for every patient with malaria
options.D: Tailoring goals and interventions to the patient's unique lifestyle and values

explanation: That's right! An individualized care plan respects the specific background, preferences, and personal goals of each unique patient. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h6)

question: How do lab staff figure out if an antibiotic can kill a specific bacterium on a test plate?

options.A: By counting how many days the culture plate sat inside the incubator
options.B: By observing if the entire agar plate changes to a bright red color
options.C: By checking the expiration date printed on the exterior box of disks
options.D: By measuring the clear ring of no growth around the antibiotic disk

explanation: That clear halo around the antibiotic disk is called the zone of inhibition. The bigger the ring, the better the drug works! [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is a major risk if a recovering patient stays on a clear liquid diet for too long?

options.A: It triggers sudden weight gain from excess fats
options.B: It causes severe high blood pressure
options.C: It permanently ruins the patient's sense of taste
options.D: It can lead to hospital-derived malnutrition due to very low calorie and nutrient content

explanation: Clear liquids are great at first, but they don't have enough energy and nutrients. Keeping patients on them too long starves their healing body! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is the biggest perk of insoluble fiber in your digestive system?

options.A: It kills harmful bacteria residing in the stomach lining
options.B: It dissolves completely to lower blood cholesterol levels
options.C: It adds bulk to stool and helps prevent constipation
options.D: It provides quick energy for high-intensity physical exercise

explanation: Insoluble fiber acts like a broom, adding bulk to waste and keeping things moving smoothly so you don't get constipated. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T009#GNS227_U1_T009_h5)

question: When does avoiding conflict turn into a real problem on a nursing unit?

options.A: When it is used during a fire drill or sudden cardiac arrest
options.B: When it is used for five minutes to let a colleague catch their breath
options.C: When it is used permanently to sweep serious problems under the rug
options.D: When it is applied to trivial, unimportant daily annoyances

explanation: Using avoidance as a permanent habit just hides serious issues until they blow up later. Problems need to be faced eventually! [learn more](GST321_U5_T4#GST321_U5_T4_h6)

question: How does increased kidney blood flow during pregnancy affect water-soluble drugs?

options.A: It causes them to accumulate dangerously in fat tissue
options.B: It completely stops the liver from breaking them down
options.C: It turns them into lipid-soluble compounds
options.D: It speeds up their elimination through the urine

explanation: Because pregnant kidneys work overtime and filter blood faster, water-soluble drugs are cleared out of the body much quicker. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is a great indicator for measuring hospital operational efficiency?

options.A: The personal religious beliefs of nursing staff
options.B: Patient waiting times and bed turnover rates
options.C: The exact brand of paint used on ward walls
options.D: The number of visitors allowed per patient daily

explanation: Waiting times and bed turnover tell us instantly how smoothly patients move through the hospital system. Excellent metrics to keep in mind! [learn more](GST321_U9_T4#GST321_U9_T4_h5)

question: An elderly patient leaks small amounts of liquid stool daily. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Bacterial food poisoning
options.B: Severe ulcerative colitis flare
options.C: Normal recovery from constipation
options.D: Fecal impaction with overflow

explanation: Liquid stool often leaks around a hard, impacted blockage in the rectum, which can trick people into thinking it is diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of mechanical digestion?

options.A: To change proteins directly into amino acids
options.B: To neutralize stomach acid before food enters the bowel
options.C: To transport nutrients through the intestinal wall
options.D: To increase the surface area of food for enzymes

explanation: Mechanical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces, which gives digestive enzymes more surface area to work on. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is a key nursing duty when giving out medications in a day hospital?

options.A: Monitoring clients for side effects like extrapyramidal symptoms
options.B: Hiding the medication from family members
options.C: Prescribing higher dosages when symptoms worsen
options.D: Allowing clients to choose whatever drug they prefer

explanation: Correct! Since clients spend a lot of time outside the hospital, nurses must watch closely for any unwanted drug reactions. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why would a surgeon leave an amputation wound open instead of stitching the skin right away?

options.A: To allow drainage and prevent trapping severe infection inside the wound
options.B: To stretch the skin flaps so they cover a larger area of bone
options.C: To give the patient time to practice moving the joint before closure
options.D: To make it easier to fit a temporary plastic cast on the bone

explanation: If there's an infection present, closing the skin immediately would trap bacteria inside and cause abscesses. Leaving it open temporarily keeps things safe! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h2)

question: Which online database is built specifically for nursing and allied health literature?

options.A: Lexicomp
options.B: Wikipedia
options.C: Google Drive
options.D: CINAHL

explanation: Spot on! CINAHL is every nursing student's best friend for finding trusted nursing journals and research. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the main job of the pudendal nerve during ejaculation?

options.A: Producing primary male sex hormones
options.B: Filtering toxins from seminal fluid
options.C: Controlling somatic pelvic floor muscles for expulsion
options.D: Stopping blood flow to the testes

explanation: Spot on! The pudendal nerve talks to the pelvic floor muscles, telling them to do those rhythmic squeezes that push semen out. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T5#GNS121_U4_T5_h2)

question: What usually happens if food travels through the small intestine much faster than normal?

options.A: Increased vitamin storage in the liver
options.B: Reduced nutrient absorption and diarrhea
options.C: Higher than normal blood sugar spikes
options.D: Enhanced breakdown of complex proteins

explanation: When food rushes through too fast, digestive enzymes and cells don't get enough time to do their job, leaving unabsorbed nutrients to pull extra water into the stool. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h6)

question: A grand multiparous woman arrives at the labor ward in active labor. What is the very first priority action you should take as the nurse?

options.A: Instruct the patient to push forcefully with every contraction
options.B: Set up an IV line and take blood for crossmatching
options.C: Prepare the patient for an immediate routine cesarean section
options.D: Administer general anesthesia to prevent any labor pain

explanation: Since heavy bleeding is a major risk for her, getting an IV line ready and having matched blood on standby before things get complicated is a true lifesaver. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T008#GNS226_U4_T008_h7)

question: What is the 'red reflex' during an ophthalmoscopic exam?

options.A: A warning light on the handle indicating low battery power
options.B: An abnormal sign of bleeding inside the front of the eye
options.C: A reddish-orange glow reflecting off the patient's retina
options.D: The natural color of the iris when exposed to bright light

explanation: The red reflex is the normal reddish-orange reflection of light seen through the pupil, confirming that the optical pathway is clear. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of cancer screening programs?

options.A: To replace traditional biopsy procedures entirely
options.B: To detect cancer or precancerous changes early
options.C: To cure late-stage metastatic disease completely
options.D: To measure the exact cost of hospital stays

explanation: Screening aims to identify disease before symptoms appear so treatment can start when it is most effective. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main internal chip that powers a microcomputer?

options.A: A massive cooling tower
options.B: A microprocessor
options.C: A dual mainframe processor
options.D: An analog wave converter

explanation: Spot on! A tiny microprocessor chip is the brain inside every microcomputer, doing all the heavy thinking. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the main job of an umbilical cord clamp?

options.A: To hold the sewing needle steady during repairs
options.B: To safely stop blood flow through the cut cord stump
options.C: To gently clear mucus from the newborn's nose
options.D: To clamp blood vessels inside the mother's uterus

explanation: Cord clamps lock tightly onto the baby's cord right after it's cut to keep the baby safe from any bleeding. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is the community nurse so vital in settings with limited resources?

options.A: They replace the need for any secondary or tertiary healthcare facilities
options.B: They have unlimited access to advanced mechanical ventilators and dialysis machines
options.C: They serve as the first line of defense to stabilize rapidly deteriorating patients before hospital transfer
options.D: They are the only healthcare workers legally permitted to perform major surgeries

explanation: Spotting danger signs early and starting care right away makes all the difference when a patient arrives at a local clinic first. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why is the home environment generally considered beneficial for a recovering child?

options.A: It removes the need for parents to monitor vital signs.
options.B: It provides the same advanced surgical tools as an operating room.
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of household infections.
options.D: It lowers psychological stress and supports normal development.

explanation: Spot on! Being around family and familiar toys helps kids feel secure, easing the fear and stress that often come with being sick. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge for surveillance in developing health systems?

options.A: Having too many computers on every hospital ward
options.B: Too many laboratories producing identical test results
options.C: Shortages of trained laboratory personnel and testing supplies
options.D: Excessive funding that overwhelms the management staff

explanation: Limited resources and trained staff make tracking and confirming infections much harder. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)

question: To get an accurate Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) measurement, what condition is needed?

options.A: A complete overnight fast of at least 12 hours
options.B: A warm environment with high physical activity
options.C: Immediate completion of a heavy physical workout
options.D: Consumption of a high-protein meal just before testing

explanation: To see what your body burns at absolute rest, we need digestion and recent activity completely out of the picture. An overnight fast does the trick! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to preserve food at home?

options.A: Exposing raw meat to open air at room temperature for several days.
options.B: Drying fruits and vegetables under the sun.
options.C: Smoking or salting fish to prevent bacterial growth.
options.D: Storing perishable items in a working refrigerator.

explanation: Correct! Leaving raw meat out in the open air lets bacteria multiply fast and ruins the food instead of saving it. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h6)

question: A patient recovering from an unsafe abortion looks quiet and won't speak to her family. What should you do first?

options.A: Call hospital security to watch for self-harm
options.B: Leave her alone in the ward until she asks for help
options.C: Demand an explanation of why she tried an illegal procedure
options.D: Sit quietly with her, listen with compassion, and promise privacy

explanation: Creating a safe, non-judgmental space builds trust and helps her share her emotional burden. Your empathy is your greatest nursing tool! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h6)

question: Why do pregnant women struggle so often with constipation?

options.A: Progesterone slows down normal bowel motility
options.B: Maternal kidneys absorb all water from the stool
options.C: The growing baby physically blocks the stomach
options.D: High protein diets stop intestinal movement

explanation: You got it! Pregnancy hormones relax smooth muscles all over the body, which unfortunately puts the brakes on digestion too. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T008#GNS227_U2_T008_h6)

question: What happens in a negative correlation between two variables?

options.A: As one variable increases, the other variable decreases
options.B: Both variables decrease at the exact same time
options.C: Both variables increase at the exact same time
options.D: There is no relationship found between the variables

explanation: Think of it like a seesaw: in a negative correlation, as one variable goes up, the other goes down. Great job thinking it through! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which ethical principle means a nurse should actively do good and help the patient?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Justice

explanation: Nailed it! 'Beneficence' comes from words meaning to do good. It's your daily push as a nurse to take positive actions that genuinely help your patients. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which special cells in your stomach lining pump out hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?

options.A: Chief cells
options.B: G cells
options.C: Mucous cells
options.D: Parietal cells

question: In social media culture, what does the popular acronym 'FoMO' stand for?

question: Why is having a clear referral pathway so important during community health screenings?

question: Why does study design matter so much when reading clinical research?

question: Why is patient-centered care an important part of reproductive health quality?

question: Which type of diaphragm bends easily in half along a central hinge to make putting it in easier?

question: What is the main goal of keeping a patient clean and fresh?

question: What is one of the biggest threats to the long-term success of mobile healthcare outreach programs?

question: Which nursing action helps build instant trust with a newly admitted PAC patient?

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to avoid bias when picking patients for a study?

question: Which part of the Glasgow Coma Scale is usually seen as the best clue to how well a patient will recover?

question: What is the main purpose of electronic communication in nursing?

question: Why does the VAPP Act break down violence into clear, specific categories like physical, emotional, and economic?

question: Which part of the brain connects the nervous system to the endocrine system?

question: Why should nurses care about a patient complaining of excessive gas?

question: A mother brings her baby for a measles shot. What should the nurse update first?

question: How do you calculate the mean (average) of a set of numbers?

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of health education in community nursing?

question: How does progesterone help protect the growing baby from the mother's immune system?

question: Why do we strictly control the movement of people inside a surgical suite?

question: A patient says their cough has lasted 10 days despite taking store-bought cough medicine, and they now have a 39°C fever. What's your best nursing advice?

question: Why are electronic monitors so helpful when looking after unstable patients?

question: What is the main purpose of a home visit in community nursing?

question: Why are the secretions of the accessory glands necessary for reproduction?

question: A patient says her urine smells strong and asks for leftover antibiotics from a friend. As her nurse, what should you tell her?

question: Why is psychological safety so important for nurses on the ward?

question: What legal charge might you face if you force medication on a clear-headed adult patient who says no?

question: When a disease is constantly present in a specific community or region, what is it called?

question: How do international treaties like the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child help shape care in Nigeria?

question: Why do healthcare workers usually resist new changes in the workplace?

question: What must be done to heat-sensitive instruments after they undergo chemical cold sterilization?

question: What term is used to describe a dangerously low fasting blood sugar level?

question: Nail clubbing (where fingertips widen and nails curve) is most commonly linked to which health issue?

question: Why is it helpful for nurses to understand basic cell biology when giving medications?

question: How do newborns primarily generate body heat when they are exposed to cold environments?

question: What is the main job of the corpus luteum during the second half of the cycle?
